verdict.rationale: A runtime probe confirms @babylonjs/core is published under Apache-2.0, a free, permissive open-source license, and the docs describe it as an 'open' engine. That means there is no per-title pricing that could be retroactively changed on shipped games. However, the pack has no evidence of the license's history over time or of any stated commitment against future changes. Community praise for backwards compatibility concerns the API, not licensing. Missing for 10: documented license/pricing history showing stability across versions, an explicit vendor commitment against retroactive license changes, independent corroboration of licensing stability.
